story.title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal

draft:
A 360‑million‑parameter model that actually *talks* like a shell.

I’ve been digging into WorldTUI, a compact model trained to emulate a terminal session. The author fed it raw command‑line logs and let the network learn the syntax, error patterns, and typical workflows. The result? A surprisingly coherent “pretend terminal” that can suggest commands, parse errors, and even simulate file system state without any external API calls.

What strikes me is how far a domain‑specific model can go with modest resources. While the big LLMs dominate headlines, a focused model like this can run locally, respects privacy, and offers instant feedback—exactly the kind of tool that could sit on a developer’s laptop and act as a silent pair‑programmer for routine tasks.

At the same time, the model still hallucinates under ambiguous prompts, reminding us that narrow AI isn’t a silver bullet. The challenge will be building guardrails that keep it helpful without letting it generate dangerous commands.

How do you see narrow, offline AI agents reshaping everyday dev workflows?
